features.title: Unified agent activity feed
features.summary: Normalizes session, communication, and jj integration events into one durable chronological feed with deduplication, bounded retention, cursor pagination, filtering, search, and provenance.
reachNarrow: click button "Observe Usage, activity, traces, jobs and hosts."
failureModes: A duplicate delivery is deduplicated by event id instead of appended twice.
Out-of-order timestamps are re-sorted on ingest.
A malformed ingest payload is rejected instead of stored.
Missing sources (no jj coordinator, no communication) leave the feed usable rather than failing.
The retained window is bounded, so old events age out predictably.

features.title: Deterministic condensation and attention visibility
features.summary: Collapses routine runs and correlated events into traceable groups while keeping errors, blocked integrations, and attention-required events individually visible; a detailed mode expands every retained event.
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Activity Timeline: Activity › attention filter
failureModes: A summary always carries the ids of its underlying events so it stays traceable.
Attention events are never folded into a routine group.

A burst of same-cause checkout sync refusals (same checkout and reason within thirty minutes) reads as one attention row with a count; its event ids stay attached and Detailed shows each one, without any retry or rebase.
Condensation is deterministic, so repeated renders produce the same feed.

features.title: Inspect verification receipts in the Activity Timeline
features.summary: Project Checks publishes a strict, bounded v2 receipt summary with its verification stage after persistence; the timeline still accepts v1, keeps peer targets, workspaces and failure text out of storage, deduplicates replay, marks failures and timeouts for attention, and opens only a currently listed Session.
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Activity Timeline: Activity › receipt detail
failureModes: Unknown schema versions and extra payload fields are rejected before the timeline stores an event.
A v1 receipt's sshTarget, workspace and failure message are dropped before storage; v2 rejects those keys.
A receipt without a recorded stage reads not-recorded instead of an inferred stage.
An archived or missing Session is reported unavailable without being revived or mutated.
A missing Activity Timeline does not prevent Project Checks from persisting its authoritative receipt.
Historical revisions are not presented as current source freshness, and configuration equivalence remains unknown.

features.title: One attention inbox for everything that needs you
features.summary: Host-owned inbox items (reason, source, subject, severity, verbs, dedupe key) in the dshfiles_attention storage domain. Providers publish, resolve or reconcile through the attention-api module; the user and the Agent list, mark done, snooze (until a time or until it changes), reopen and mute a source; provider verbs such as Answer are handed to the owning plugin. Browsers follow a live changed event carrying the Needs you count.
features.currentSurface: Host contract: attention-api module and attention_* agent tools
failureModes: A repeat with the same source and dedupe key merges into one item instead of stacking; an unchanged repeat writes nothing.

A changed repeat lifts a snooze-until-change; it lifts a Done only when the headline changed (reason, severity, verbs, choices, subject), so a refreshed detail updates the item in place; a timed snooze holds until its time.
A resolved item reopens only when its source publishes it again; Reopen on a resolved item is refused with the reason.
Browsers and agents cannot publish, resolve or reconcile; those calls are refused as provider-only.
A provider verb with no loaded owner returns an outcome telling the user to open the thread instead of failing silently.
Info items never reach the inbox; they become one Activity log entry.
Closed items are pruned after seven days and the store is bounded at 2000 items.

A Ready item left unopened for 72 hours (no provider change, reopen or ended snooze) moves to Done on a ten-minute sweep; Reopen brings it back for another 72 hours, and Needs you and Failed items never expire.

externalDependencies.boundary: Provider through the attention-api module (publish/resolve/reconcile, dshfiles/attention/act); the inbox never reads its storage.

features.title: Inbox page with one Needs you badge
features.summary: An Inbox entry in the left navigation opens one page with Needs you and Other tabs (plus Snoozed, Done and Muted when they hold items). Each row leads with the thread or item it is about, then the sentence saying what it is about and its detail, with one direct action (Review thread, Open thread, or Open <subject>) and its verbs inline: answer choices, Land, Done, Snooze and Mute source, with Reopen and Unmute on the history tabs. Land asks first, showing what will land, and an item that can Land also offers Review, which opens the thread's Changes view (dshx Changes contract). Other notes that Ready items left unopened for three days move to Done. Needs you leads with one Resume all for every open item whose provider marks it resumable. The nav glyph carries the only badge, the Needs you count, and can raise opt-in browser alerts for new Needs you items (a question or a failure): the thread's title is the notification title, the question or the failure (with its first recovery line) the body, and a click opens that item's thread or page. Option-J (Jump to next waiting, listed in Settings › Key bindings and the palette) opens the next Needs you item's thread, cycling; with nothing waiting it opens the Inbox.
failureModes: An archived or missing thread is reported unavailable with a recovery hint instead of being reopened.

features.title: Open an Inbox item's source in one click
features.summary: Every Inbox row whose subject another page owns offers its own direct action: Review thread for a finished turn, Open thread for a thread subject (an archived one says so), and Open <subject> for a page such as a backlog item, which opens that item in the Backlog page. features.title: Push blocking Inbox items to a device
features.summary: Below the in-tab alerts, the Inbox offers Push blocking items to this device. Turning it on asks for notification permission, registers a service worker the Host serves from its own origin (/dshfiles-web-push/sw.js, scope its own folder, so it controls no page), subscribes the browser with the Host's VAPID key and records the device. The Host keeps its VAPID keys and every device's subscription in the dshfiles_web_push storage domain and pushes each new Needs you or Failed item once to every device (Ready items never push; the first read after a Host start only seeds, so a restart replays nothing), encrypted aes128gcm with Node crypto. A click opens the item's thread. A subscription the push service forgot (404/410) is dropped; another failure stays on the device with what to do. Send test proves the path. On an iPhone, push needs DSH on the Home Screen (iOS 16.4+); the Inbox says so. Agents list devices (inbox_push_devices), send a test (inbox_push_test) and remove a device with confirm: true (inbox_push_remove); a device subscribes only itself, so subscribing has no agent tool.
